clinician.final_diagnosis: A diagnosis of erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP) secondary to MDS was made.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 73-year-old man with a 2-year history of sun sensitivity, burning pain, and crusting skin lesions on sun-exposed areas presented to the dermatology clinic. Clinical examination revealed thickened, lichenified skin with fresh blisters, crusts, indented scars, and milia formation on the dorsa of the hands, neck, and face. Laboratory testing showed a massive increase in plasma total porphyrins and free protoporphyrin. The patient had a known history of myelodysplastic syndrome with multilineage dysplasia (MDS-MLD) diagnosed 6 years prior.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with sun sensitivity, burning pain, and crusting skin lesions on face, hands, and fingertips for 2 years.
Clinical examination revealed thickened, lichenified skin with fresh blister, numerous crusts, indented scars, and milia formation on the dorsa of the hands and some on the back of the neck and face.
Plasma fluorescence scan was positive and revealed a massive increase in total porphyrins at 33.9 umol/L (normal < 1.30) and free protoporphyrin 30 umol/L (normal < 0.20).
Patient has a known prior history of myelodysplastic syndrome with multilineage dysplasia (MDS-MLD) diagnosed 6 years ago.
